prerequisites: Fundamentals of Engineering Economics (with a particular focus on cost structures and the production function)

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the role of various corporate functions and their interdependencies, as well as their interactions with external nodes within the supply chain in which the focal firm operates
Analyze and interpret the architecture of technical-economic supply chains, demonstrating conceptual and operational mastery of core supply chain processes
Design and critically evaluate alternative supply chain configurations
Understand and apply decision-support tools typical of supply chain management (e.g., supplier selection and evaluation, make-or-buy decisions)

syllabus_topics: Characteristics of goods and services, servitization trend
Value chain activities of the focal firm
Main organizational functions and interactions within the broader value system
Industrial costs and economies of scale, volume, scope, and breadth
Concept of process and system optimization, necessity of trade-offs in decision-making
Demand forecasting across different planning horizons (long, medium, and short term; e.g., capacity creation vs. capacity adjustment, master planning, and production scheduling)
Manufacturing processes and their impact on production costs
Importance of the circular economy in supply chains
Fundamentals of supply chain risk management

assessment_methods.method: Oral Exam (two questions, discussion of student work)

assessment_rules: Passing the written portion (grade ">= 18/30") is required to proceed to the oral exam. The written exam accounts for 60% of the final grade, and the oral exam accounts for 40%. Students may be exempt from the written final exam by passing two voluntary midterm tests. If a student fails at most one midterm test, they may make it up during an official exam session by retaking only the corresponding section of the written exam. The oral exam must be taken in the same exam session in which the written portion is passed or the failed midterm is successfully made up.

Antoldi F., (2012), Economia ed organizzazione aziendale, McGraw Hill, II edizione
